title: Micro-theme system for data cards and tiny visuals in dark console
creator: Lena Chen
description: Create a micro-theme layer and token mapping strategy specifically for compact data cards, inline mini-visuals (tiny bars, micro sparklines, KPI chips), and dense table row states when the console is in dark or adaptive themes. Goal is to preserve perceptual contrast for data marks and interactive affordances while keeping brand color fidelity for customer themes.
background: Design tokens and component overrides currently handle primary UI surfaces and forms, but we see regressions in legibility and chart mark visibility when brand themes or high-contrast dark modes are applied. Product teams are shipping compact KPI cards and table-embedded visuals more frequently; these small marks lose meaning in some theme combinations. Engineering has also added per-component color props for charts which introduced variance that bypasses token guardrails.
scope:
- Define a micro-theme token subset (3–5 tokens) that components can consume for tiny visuals and data marks.
- Map micro-theme tokens across existing brand palettes and adaptive dark fallbacks.
- Provide component-level override patterns for DataCard, MiniChart, TableRowCompact, KPIChip.
- Accessibility checks for WCAG contrast on small UI marks and icons.
- Hand off to component library with code examples and visual regression test cases.
out_of_scope:
- Global brand palette redesign.
- Major runtime changes to charting library internals.
- Full refresh of all console components (only the listed compact components).
acceptance_criteria: A micro-theme token set (micro.surface, micro.mark, micro.accent, micro.interactive, micro.dim) defined and documented in the token spec.
Token mappings exist for all active brand themes (Default, BrandA, BrandB) and for adaptive dark and deep-dark variants.
Component-level examples updated: DataCard (compact), KPIChip, MiniChart (inline), TableRowCompact — each using micro tokens and passing visual regressions.
Automated contrast checks added to the token pipeline for small mark sizes (1–2px strokes, 8px text).
Design review approved by PM and accessibility lead (sign-off in comments).

design_notes: Prefer semantic micro tokens instead of one-off hex values so component authors get consistent contrast helpers.
micro.surface should be anchored to the underlying surface elevation but offset by 4–8% luminance for tiny marks to avoid flattening.
micro.mark variants: strong, muted, success, danger — choose hues that remain distinguishable on dark backgrounds when reduced to 1px strokes.
For brand-accented data marks, create a desaturated fallback (brandAccent-desat) used in dark mode to preserve brand signal without breaking contrast.
Transition animations for interactive micro-affordances (hover focus) should use alpha/overlay tokens instead of hue shifts to avoid color banding on low-bit-depth displays.
Provide recommended stroke widths and anti-aliasing hints to engineers for canvas/SVG rendering contexts.

decisions: Create 5 micro tokens (micro.surface, micro.mark, micro.accent, micro.interactive, micro.dim).
Micro tokens will be mapped per brand theme and have an adaptive dark variant computed by the token pipeline rather than manual per-theme edits.
Expose micro tokens to components via token API and allow opt-in overrides at the component instance level with clear precedence rules.
Automated visual contrast checks will rasterize 1x and 2x snapshots and verify against WCAG-derived thresholds for small marks.
